STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a rim band and a flat centre, with no inner wall or bowl shadow. Flat square plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This plate looks medium-sized, so about 24 cm.
b) Reference: the plate is roughly 2.5 to 3 times the length of the cucumber/zucchini slices, which are about 10-12 cm long. Estimating across the plate at roughly 2.3 zucchini lengths gives about 24-26 cm.
Reconciled width: about 24 cm square. Area = 24 x 24 = 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:

- Roasted/fried root vegetable pieces (white cubes with browned edges, likely parsnip or similar): about 6 pieces, each around 3 x 3 x 2.5 cm, roughly 20 g each. Footprint about 10 x 10 cm = 100 cm² and a single layer ~2.5 cm thick, but they are sparse, so use about 70 g total.
- Yellow and green zucchini/squash slices: a sparse arrangement covering about 60 cm² in a flat layer about 1 cm thick. Volume ~60 ml, density 0.6 g/ml gives about 40 g. Summing the slices, use about 45 g.
- Couscous (yellow, with herbs and bits of vegetable): a mound about 10 x 8 cm, footprint ~80 cm². Average thickness about 1.5 cm (mound averages about half of a peak of ~3 cm). Volume ~120 ml, bulk density 0.8 g/ml gives about 95 g. Cooked grain with visible saffron/turmeric colouring and some vegetable bits, so use about 100 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No obvious base layer is hidden beneath the couscous; it sits directly on the plate. No additional items added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Roasted root vegetable: about 90 kcal/100 g (starchy, lightly oiled).
- Zucchini/squash, cooked: about 25 kcal/100 g.
- Couscous, cooked, with oil and vegetables: about 130 kcal/100 g.

Totals: roughly 70 g root vegetable (63 kcal), 45 g squash (11 kcal), 100 g couscous (130 kcal). Total about 215 g and about 205 kcal.
